audit_method: Same-agent exact comparison against the frozen source, adjacent definitions, formal notation and referenced earlier results within that revision. No claim about current upstream master is made.

corrections.finding: The string presentation applies its operations to natural-number exponents rather than to elements of the stated string domain.
corrections.handling: Used the actual string-domain elements a^n and a^m as the arguments of addition and multiplication, with an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The domain is {a}*, and the displayed outputs and claimed isomorphism require operations on strings in that domain.

corrections.finding: The example omits an interpretation for < even though it purports to give an L_A-structure isomorphic to the standard model.
corrections.handling: Added the transported order relation a^n<a^m iff n<m and disclosed the addition in an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: L_A contains <, and an isomorphism claim requires preservation of that relation as well as the listed operations.

corrections.finding: The existentially bound witness x is missing from the binary proof predicate in the displayed inconsistency claim.
corrections.handling: Restored x as the first proof-predicate argument and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The consistency formula earlier in the same paragraph displays the binary predicate with x and the contradiction code as its two arguments.

corrections.finding: The surjectivity explanation says that an omitted element is outside the domain of s, although s is defined on all of M.
corrections.handling: Used range rather than domain and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: For s:M→M\{z}, failure of surjectivity means that an element of the codomain is absent from the range.

corrections.finding: The compactness proof chooses the greatest indexed disequality in a finite fragment without handling a fragment containing none.
corrections.handling: Chose an index larger than every one occurring and explicitly used m=0 when the index set is empty, with an adjacent keyed note.

mathematical_delta.added_case: no added disequality occurs in Gamma_0

corrections.controlling_evidence: A finite subset of Gamma may consist only of sentences from true arithmetic, so a greatest added-disequality index need not exist.

corrections.finding: Compactness supplies a model but the proposition specifically claims an enumerable non-standard model.
corrections.handling: Applied the earlier downward Löwenheim–Skolem theorem to choose an enumerable model and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The expanded language is countable, and the cited earlier theorem supplies the countable-model conclusion not obtained from compactness alone.

corrections.finding: The parenthetical gloss of the transported sum is not closed before multiplication is introduced.
corrections.handling: Closed the sum gloss before introducing multiplication and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The parallel successor, sum and product glosses each form a separate parenthetical explanation.

corrections.finding: A case in the K example uses b even though the domain has only the one added element a.
corrections.handling: Used a, as required by the domain and the following calculation, and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: Domain K is N∪{a}; the displayed case immediately below also computes with a.

corrections.finding: The a-case ends with b plus an unbound y rather than with b plus a.
corrections.handling: Replaced y by a in the final term and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The left side of this row and the operation table both identify the case as y=a.

corrections.finding: The linearity formula has one extra closing parenthesis and one extra closing bracket.
corrections.handling: Balanced the formula delimiters and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: Two quantifiers and the one outer grouping parenthesis determine the required closing delimiters.

corrections.finding: The proposition gives every element a predecessor, contradicting Q_2 at zero.
corrections.handling: Excluded zero and restricted the later block proof to non-standard elements, with an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: Q_2 says zero is not a successor; the block argument only applies to non-standard elements and remains valid under the corrected claim.

corrections.finding: The averaging proof abruptly uses an undeclared op-plus symbol instead of the model-addition notation fixed for the section.
corrections.handling: Used nsplus in all four positions and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The preceding sentence and every earlier model calculation in the section use nsplus for interpreted addition.

corrections.finding: The explanation calls the block order denumerable without assuming that the model is enumerable.
corrections.handling: Added the needed enumerability hypothesis while preserving the following comparison of two enumerable models, with an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: An arbitrary model of PA may be uncountable; a partition into finite-or-countable successor blocks need not itself be denumerable without this hypothesis.

corrections.finding: The second relation comprehension forms pairs with x but binds an unrelated n.
corrections.handling: Bound x, matching the ordered pair and the earlier definition of K, with an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: The relation in the referenced K example contains every pair <x,a> with x in its domain.

corrections.finding: The claimed bijection sends positive n to n+1 and therefore omits 0 and 1 from its range.
corrections.handling: Used g(n)=n−1 for n>0, which is the bijection required by all following transported interpretations, and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: With g(0)=a, the positive inputs must enumerate all naturals; g(1)=0 also explains why 1 becomes the transported zero constant below.

corrections.finding: Tennenbaum's theorem is stated as literal uniqueness of N rather than uniqueness up to isomorphism.
corrections.handling: Stated that every computable PA model is standard, hence isomorphic to N, and added an adjacent keyed note.
corrections.controlling_evidence: Computable permutations of N transport the standard interpretations to distinct computable structures on the same domain; Tennenbaum rules out non-standard computable models.
